    Tender Gluten-Free Blueberry Muffins (Almond & Oat Flour)

    By Alanna Taylor-Tobin on Jul 24, 2026 / 15 Comments Jump to Recipe

    Listen to audio version of this article
    Sponsored by
    0:00 / 6:07
    Instaread

    My ideal gluten-free blueberry muffins are moist, tender, and loaded with jammy berries. I use a blend of alternative flours – sweet rice, oat, and almond flours with a touch of tapioca starch – for big flavor and a hearty, soft texture. These take 20 minutes of active time to make and will emerge from the oven after a 25-minute bake with golden, domed tops worthy of any bakery.

    Blueberry muffins are a classic, which is why I've been working on my ideal for over a decade! I first shared a corn flour blueberry muffin recipe in my award-winning cookbook Alternative Baker. But I don't always have corn flour in my pantry, so I created this version using my most-used flours, all of which I've written about in my gluten-free flours guide for bakers of all levels.

    These muffins are perfectly balanced and not overly sweet, trading cake-like fluff for a tender, deeply satisfying crumb that feels substantial without being heavy. I love having a dozen of these fruit-packed quickbreads on hand for a post-lunch snack, toasted and smeared with a touch of quick honey butter or a dollop of homemade lemon curd. And yes, they freeze beautifully too!

    Gluten-Free Flour Power

    Rather than use gluten-free all-purpose flour, which I've found can give baked goods a chalky or gritty texture, I use a custom blend for a smooth crumb with a wheat-like mouthfeel. Almond flour adds moisture and tenderness, oat flour contributes a soft, velvety crumb, sweet rice flour gives the crumb a pleasant bounciness, and tapioca flour makes the dough stretchy enough to catch pockets of air and floof.

    They're loaded with 2 cups of berries which bake into jammy, indigo pockets, plus vanilla extract and lemon zest and juice to make the low-acid berries pop with flavor.

    Like my almond and oat flour banana muffin recipe, I found that using oil rather than butter keeps the crumb extra tender; bonus that the batter can be whisked together in one bowl. A bit of cultured dairy adds moisture and lift; I especially love using creme fraiche or sour cream for super-moist middles, but Greek yogurt or dairy-free yogurts work well, too. When I make these for my Celiac friends, I'll use sorghum flour instead of oat flour, and Forager cashew yogurt for the dairy, which actually makes them bake up extra floofy. I made the batch shown in these photos with crème fraiche and sorghum flour.

    Stir, Scoop, Bake, Yum

    Bojon appétit! If you're hungry for more, check out my award-winning gluten-free baking cookbook Alternative Baker or subscribe to my free, spamless newsletter to hear from me every week or so.

    Tender Gluten-Free Blueberry Muffins (Almond & Oat Flour)

    Print Recipe Pin Recipe
    My ideal gluten-free blueberry muffins are moist, tender, and loaded with jammy berries. I use a blend of alternative flours – sweet rice, oat, and almond flours with a touch of tapioca starch – for big flavor and a hearty, soft texture. These take 20 minutes of active time to make and will emerge from the oven after a 25-minute bake with golden, domed tops worthy of any bakery.
    Alanna Taylor-Tobin
    Prep Time: 20 minutes minutes
    Cook Time: 25 minutes minutes
    Chilling Time: 20 minutes minutes
    Total: 1 hour hour 5 minutes minutes
    Servings: 12 muffins

    Ingredients

    Wet ingredients

    • ½ cup (100 g) granulated sugar, plus 1 teaspoon for sprinkling on top
    • 3 large eggs
    • 9 tablespoons (110 g) neutral oil (I use Suncoco oil, but sunflower and grapeseed are good choices too)
    • ¾ cup (170 g) creme fraiche (shown here), sour cream, or full-fat Greek yogurt (to make these dairy-free I like to use equal parts Forager cashew yogurt and Forager Greek yogurt)
    • 1 ½ teaspoons gluten-free vanilla extract
    • finely grated zest of 1 small lemon
    • 2 teaspoons fresh lemon juice
    • 2 cups (260 g) fresh or frozen blueberries (plus 1 tablespoon oat or sorghum flour for tossing)

    Dry ingredients

    • 1 cup + 2 tablespoons (112 g) gluten-free oat flour (or ⅞ cup / 112 g sorghum flour, shown here)
    • ¾ cup (84 g) blanched almond flour
    • ¾ cup (115 g) sweet rice flour
    • 3 tablespoons (23 g) tapioca flour
    • 2 teaspoons baking powder
    • ¾ teaspoon baking soda
    • 1 teaspoon fine sea salt

    Equipment

    • 1 muffin tin
    • 12 paper muffin liners

    Instructions

    Batter

    • In a large bowl, whisk together the ½ cup of sugar and eggs. Whisk in the oil, then the crème fraiche (or sour cream/yogurt), vanilla, lemon zest, and lemon juice.
    • In a small bowl, toss the blueberries to coat them with 1 tablespoon of oat or sorghum flour.
    • Sift the dry ingredients into the wet ingredients, stir until almost combined, then fold in the blueberries to distribute them evenly.

    Shape and Bake

    • Divide the batter between 12 standard muffin tins lined with paper liners; the batter will nearly fill the muffin tins to the top.
    • Refrigerate while you preheat the oven to 375ºF, about 20 minutes – this will make the muffins dome nicely.
    • Sprinkle the muffins evenly with the remaining 1 teaspoon sugar (or more if you like a sweeter crunch on top!) Bake in the upper third of the oven until the tops are golden and a toothpick comes out with a few moist crumbs, 25-35 minutes.
    • Enjoy warm or at room temperature.

    Storage

    • I like to store these in a covered container at room temperature for up to 1 day, then in the fridge for up to a week. These freeze well – I currently have some stashed in my freezer for a rainy day!

    Notes

    • Sometimes when I want to take these over-the-top I'll sprinkle the batter with a batch of the almond flour streusel from my rhubarb muffins. 
    • I especially love how moist these muffins turn out made with sour cream or crème fraiche. But they also work well made with Greek yogurt, they just have slightly firmer texture. 
    • When serving these a day or two after baking, I like to pop them in the toaster oven to refresh for a few minutes until warmed through, then I slice them in half and top them with a little homemade honey butter or silky lemon curd. 
    • I recommend measuring ingredients by weight for ease and accuracy. This is my favorite kitchen scale. But if you only have measuring cups, be sure to use the dip and sweep method for measuring flours. 
    • Need more ingredient subs? Leave a comment and I'll get back to you ASAP.
